item.title: Lusin and pseudo-Lusin theorems for monotone measures: necessary conditions, conjugate duality and a correction of a theorem of Castaldo and Marinacci
item.description: arXiv:2611.28039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lusin's theorem for monotone measures has been studied mainly through sufficient conditions. Here we study it from the side of necessary conditions and of conjugate duality. We show that, for an arbitrary monotone measure on a metric space, the Lusin property with closed sets implies regularity, and the Lusin property with compact sets implies order continuity and tightness. Consequently, for finite submeasures the Lusin property is characterized by order continuity on compact spaces, and the compact-set Lusin property is characterized by order continuity on Polish spaces. We then consider a pseudo-Lusin property, in which the Lusin set is required to have almost full measure, and observe that it is exactly the Lusin property of the conjugate measure. For finite monotone measures whose conjugate is subadditive, a class including supermodular capacities, belief functions and coherent lower probabilities, the pseudo-Lusin property is equivalent to continuity from below on compact spaces, and so is its compact-set version on Polish spaces. As an application, we give a corrected form, together with its converse, of a Lusin-type theorem of Castaldo and Marinacci whose original statement was refuted by Wiesel. Several examples, one of them based on meagre sets, show that the hypotheses cannot be omitted.
item.dc:creator: Duc Toan Truong, Kiet Ho, Thanh Ngo Vo Ke, Cuong Le Quoc, Tran Nhat Luan

item.title: Approximation by classical summability methods in variable Lebesgue spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.28041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate approximation by Fej\'er and N\"orlund means with respect to the Walsh system in variable Lebesgue spaces. We prove that the Fej\'er means are uniformly bounded on the weighted space $L^1_w[0,1)$ if and only if $w\in A_1(\mathcal{D})$. We then apply Rubio de Francia extrapolation to show that both means are uniformly bounded on $L^{p(\cdot)}[0,1)$ with $1\le p_-\le p_+<\infty$ if and only if $p(\cdot)\in\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{D})$. Finally, we estimate the approximation errors via the modulus of smoothness and deduce convergence rates for variable Lipschitz classes.
item.dc:creator: Tengiz Kopaliani, Alina Shalukhina, George Tephnadze

item.title: Dynamic Combinatorics of Quantum Modes in an Inverted Fock Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.28043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An inversive approach to the combinatorics of Fock space in quantum field theory is proposed. The traditional description of Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac systems is based on distributing indistinguishable quanta (particles) over energy states (modes). The present model introduces a methodological inversion: identical wave modes of a fixed frequency are declared as invariant elements (balls), while discrete occupancy numbers (Fock numbers) act as bins (spatial axes). It is shown that the time evolution of a quantum system governed by elastic interactions represents a trajectory of geometric hops of modes across occupancy axes. This approach eliminates ultraviolet divergences without introducing artificial regulators, visually differentiates thermodynamic quantum statistics, and rigorously derives Planck's entropy and the spectral characteristics of coherent laser systems.
item.dc:creator: E. A. Isayeva

item.title: Quantum Reversal of Dialectics: Inversion of Qualities and Occupation Numbers in Statistical Physics
item.description: arXiv:2611.28045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a conceptual approach to quantum statistics called the inversion of qualities. Inspired by dialectical philosophy and the distinction between quality and quantity, the approach interprets quantum modes as qualitative characteristics and occupation numbers as quantitative measures of their realization. The paper examines the relation between occupation numbers and the statistical behavior of bosons and fermions. It discusses the role of combinatorial reasoning in describing quantum states, the harmonic oscillator, and Planck's black-body radiation formula. The mean occupation number of a bosonic mode is derived using the standard geometric-series method. The approach is compared with the Fock-space formalism and second quantization. Its conceptual scope and limitations are discussed through examples involving electromagnetic modes, phonons, and the hydrogen atom. The proposed inversion is presented as a philosophical interpretation of established quantum-statistical formalism rather than a replacement for standard quantum mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Elmira A. Isayeva

item.title: A Matrix-Valued Quotient and a Compatible Bilinear Product on Euclidean Vector Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.28061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a matrix-valued quotient and a compatible bilinear product on finite-dimensional Euclidean vector spaces. The quotient is constructed from a bilinear matrix-valued map satisfying a prescribed vector transport identity. We investigate its algebraic structure and establish uniqueness results under orthogonal equivariance and additional structural conditions. We also derive a variational characterization based on the Frobenius norm and examine the spectral properties of the associated matrices, including their determinants and invertibility conditions. The two-dimensional construction is related to complex arithmetic, while the three-dimensional formulation admits a representation using skew-symmetric matrices. The results clarify the relationship between vector transport, matrix algebra, and Euclidean geometry, and extend the framework introduced in our earlier work on vector division and multiplication.
item.dc:creator: J. Enrique H. Ramirez

item.title: Scalability and Performance Trade-offs Between Q-Learning and Parallel Intensified Simulated Annealing in Flexible Job Shop Scheduling
item.description: arXiv:2611.28062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article presents a controlled comparison of tabular Q-learning (QL) and Parallelized Simulated Annealing with Intensification (PISA) for the Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP).
item.dc:creator: Robert L Burdett, Paul Corry

item.title: Covering hypercubic grids by polygonal trails: capacity bounds and the optimum for $P(4,3)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.28108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical nine-dot puzzle asks for a polygonal trail through a square grid using as few segments as possible. We study its higher-dimensional analogue on $P(n,k):=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}^k$ for integers $n,k\ge2$, allowing arbitrary real vertices and unrestricted segment directions, and denote the minimum number of segments by $h(n,k)$. For $n\ge3$ and $k\ge2$, we give a geometric proof of the previously stated capacity bound: a trail of $r\ge1$ segments meets at most $1+r(n-1)$ grid points. Refinements of this bound, combined with exhaustive finite checks, establish $h(4,3)=23$ and $h(5,3)\ge32$. We also exhibit a $22$-segment trail through $63$ points of $P(4,3)$, the maximum possible, and a $23$-segment covering trail contained in $[0,4]^3$, which settles the corresponding box-constrained problem. The general capacity theorem, a large-grid lower bound refuting a previously proposed formula for $h(n,k)$, and the boxed construction are verified by the Lean 4 kernel, whereas the finite exclusions use native reflection and additionally trust the native compiler and runtime. A companion technical note provides the computational specification and reproducible proof artifacts.
item.dc:creator: Aldo Roberto Pessolano, Marco Rip\`a

item.title: Every friend of 10 has at least eleven distinct prime factors
item.description: arXiv:2611.28126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A friend of $10$ is a positive integer $N\neq 10$ such that $\sigma(N)/N=\sigma(10)/10=9/5$. Whether one exists is an open problem. Thackeray proved that a friend of $10$ has at least $10$ distinct prime factors. We describe a computer-assisted proof that it has at least $11$. The proof is an exhaustive search over sets of primes, carried out by a recursive certifier written in PARI/GP, which extends the open-source project caioross/solitary10. The new ingredients are a split of ``almost tight'' nodes that avoids enumerating the smallest unknown prime, a treatment of nodes with three or more unknown primes by a saturation dichotomy, a counting rule for unfactored cofactors of cyclotomic values, and the correction of a soundness gap in the earlier closure rule. The certification run for $\omega=10$ visited $157{,}210{,}962$ nodes in $11.4$ hours on $12$ threads. As a consequence, a friend of $10$ would be larger than $10^{38}$.
item.dc:creator: Filip Fifka

item.title: Fishburn Numbers Count Homogeneous Games
item.description: arXiv:2611.28133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a new combinatorial interpretation for Fishburn numbers, in that they count the number of homogeneous games; specifically homogeneous games without dummy players, which we show extends to homogeneous games via the partial sums of Fishburn numbers. In doing so, we settle two conjectures commented in the OEIS A189359 entry, and finish off by providing some immediate consequences on homogeneous game counts; including an asymptotic formula and congruences.
item.dc:creator: Marnix Joris

item.title: Sharp Simultaneous Asymptotic Expansions for Sample-Mean Operators from Natural Exponential Families
item.description: arXiv:2611.28165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of positive linear operators constructed from sample means of natural exponential families parametrized by their means. We show that the variance function $V$ determines the entire hierarchy of cumulants, central moments, and coefficient differential operators $A_r[V]$ governing the asymptotic expansions. The cumulants satisfy the recursion $\kappa_{j+1}=V\kappa_j'$, whereas the central moments are expressed in terms of partial Bell polynomials. Quantitative expansions of arbitrary order, uniform on compact subsets of the mean domain, are obtained. We also establish simultaneous expansions for the derivatives $(L_nf)^{(\ell)}$, with an explicit remainder estimate in terms of the modulus of continuity of the highest derivative. We prove that $C^{2N+\ell}$-smoothness is sufficient for the expansion of the derivative of order $\ell$ up to and including the term of order $n^{-N}$. The Gauss-Weierstrass operators show that, within the scale of spaces $C^m$, this smoothness threshold cannot generally be lowered and that the order of the modulus-of-continuity term is optimal. The general framework is applied to the Bernstein, Sz\'asz-Mirakjan, Baskakov, Post-Widder, and Gauss-Weierstrass operators.
item.dc:creator: Oleksandr Volkov

item.title: Density Regularity from Derivative Growth of Cauchy-Type Integrals
item.description: arXiv:2611.28166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the relationship between the behavior of the derivative of a Cauchy-type integral near the curve of integration and the regularity of its density. We consider Jordan curves and Jordan arcs composed of finitely many regular $C^1$ arcs meeting at nondegenerate angles. For a Cauchy-type integral with continuous density, we establish an inverse estimate: if the growth of its derivative off the curve is controlled by a continuous integrable function of the distance to the curve that is nonincreasing near zero, then the modulus of continuity of the density at scale $h$ is bounded by the integral of this majorant over $(0,h)$. As a consequence, we prove that power-law decay of the derivative as the curve is approached forces the density to be constant. For Jordan curves, combining the inverse and direct estimates yields a criterion for H\"older continuity of the density in terms of the growth of the derivative of the integral. We then apply this criterion to characterize the H\"older regularity of analytic functions in bounded Jordan domains whose boundaries satisfy the same geometric assumptions. The proof relies on uniformly transverse shifts of local subarcs and a symmetric jump formula.
item.dc:creator: Oleksandr Volkov

item.title: Generalized Fundamental Theorem of Calculus on a Regular Time Scale
item.description: arXiv:2611.28187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main objectives of this paper can be summarized as, giving a fundamental theorem on a regular time scale as well as illustrating that applications are possible on a homogeneous time scale.
item.dc:creator: Billur Kaymak\c{c}alan, Yeter \c{S}ahiner, \c{S}eyda Y{\i}ld{\i}z, Emre Deniz Y{\i}lmaz

item.title: Linear and non-linear integro-differential equations with variable coefficients and Sonin kernels
item.description: arXiv:2611.29047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study linear and non-linear integro-differential equations, with Sonin and absolutely continuous kernels, and with variable coefficients which are either integrable or continuous functions. In the linear case, for all cases, the unique solution is given explicitly by a convergent infinite series involving compositions of convolutions of the kernels and the variable coefficients. Many examples are provided. For the non-linear case, the existence and uniqueness are established under a suitable condition in the non-linear term. The analytic solution is given by the limit of the iterative sequence found from the method of successive approximations. The exact analytical expressions for several problems are found by computing the iterative sequences that approximate the solution.
item.dc:creator: Joel E. Restrepo, Sebastian Nu\~nez

item.title: Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli with multilinear weights
item.description: arXiv:2611.29075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the average distribution of primes up to $x$ in arithmetic progressions to moduli $q$ larger than $\sqrt{x}$, where $q = q_1 \cdots q_n$ ($n \geqslant 2$) with conveniently sized divisors $q_1, \ldots, q_n$ and the average is weighted by an arbitrary divisor-bounded multilinear weight. Specifically, we show that the primes up to $x$ are equidistributed in the residue class $a \pmod{q_1 q_2}$ on average over moduli $q_1 q_2$ as large as $x^{8/15 - \varepsilon}$ when the average is weighted by a bilinear weight and the sizes of $q_1$ and $q_2$ lie in an explicit region, improving the exponent $9/17$ for bilinear weights obtained recently by Li. The new ingredient here is an estimate for the Type-II convolution sums with both factors have size about $x^{1/2}$. With this estimate, the level of distribution $8/15$ in the bilinear case is no longer limited by the Type-II sums but by the Type-I$_3$ sums, or the current range in the ternary divisor problem. We also get further improvements for $n \geqslant 3$ using a simple form of Harman's sieve together with various arithmetic information, including the Type-II estimate mentioned above. We group the divisors $q_1, \ldots, q_n$ in different ways in order to use arithmetic information more efficiently. Specifically, we reach $x^{145/266 - \varepsilon}$ for trilinear weights, $x^{457/814 - \varepsilon}$ for quadrilinear weights and $x^{3614/6353 - \varepsilon}$ for quintilinear weights. As the number of divisors increases, the exponent approaches $4/7$, the long-standing result with well-factorable weights proved by Bombieri, Friedlander and Iwaniec.
item.dc:creator: Runbo Li

item.title: A Majorana Relativistic Quantum Spectral Approach to the Riemann Hypothesis in (1+1)-Dimensional Rindler Spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2503.09644v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a Hilbert--P\'olya approach to the Riemann zeta function via a Mellin--Barnes integral for massive Majorana modes in $(1+1)$-dimensional Rindler spacetime. The boost spectrum is continuous on the full wedge and discrete with a reflecting wall. Summing positive momentum modes on a transverse circle yields $\zeta(2s)$ in the radial Mellin transform. Building on our one-sided Ces\`aro criterion for additive correlations of $\Lambda(n)-1$, we assign each prime $p$ a chiral channel of optical length $\tfrac12\log p$. Its $k$th return at $u=k\log p$ carries weight $\log p$. The centered correlation obeys $C(u)\le C(0)$ for all real $u$ exactly when the Riemann hypothesis (RH) holds. For a Majorana oscillator with linear mass profile, a bounded self-adjoint function of its Hamiltonian assigns period $kT_1$ to mode pair $k$. The first $n$ pairs have least common period $T_n=T_1\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,n)$, so $\log(T_n/T_{n-1})=\Lambda(n)$ for $n\ge2$. Set $m=\lceil\sqrt{x}\rceil$, $N=\lfloor mx\rfloor$, and $\psi(y)=\sum_{n\le y}\Lambda(n)$. The signed revival mean $A(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}(N/j-\psi(N/j))$ satisfies $A(x)=R(x)+o(\sqrt{x})$, where $R(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)(x/n-1)-x\log x+(1+\gamma_{\mathrm E})x$. At each zeta zero $\rho$ of multiplicity $d$ with $\Re(\rho)>1/2$, the meromorphic continuation of $\int_2^\infty A(x)x^{-s-1}\,dx$ has a simple pole of residue $d/[\rho(1-\rho)]$. For fixed $\lambda>1$, $1/2<\theta<\Re(\rho)$ and $K>0$, the Kaczorowski--Pintz theorem gives $A(x)>Kx^\theta$ at some $x\in[Y,Y^\lambda]$ for all large $Y$. Thus RH follows if for each $\varepsilon>0$ there is a $C_\varepsilon$ with $A(x)\le C_\varepsilon x^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ throughout $[Y,Y^\lambda]$ for arbitrarily large $Y$. For $\lambda=3/2$, the independent theta-lift estimate reported by Alp\"oge and Claude for $G=R$ gives this bound for $A$.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Tamburini (Rotonium - Quantum Computing, Le Village by CA, Padova, Italy)

item.title: Quantile-Based Skewness for Fuzzy Numbers With Probabilistic Foundations: An Application in Portfolio Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2602.20183v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article quantifies asymmetry under imprecision by introducing a probabilistic interpretation for fuzzy numbers and a non-moment based skewness coefficient derived from it. The coefficient adapts classical quantile-based skewness measures (Bowley, Kelley, and Groeneveld-Meeden) to the $\alpha$-cut representation of fuzzy numbers. Existing studies typically modify the classical Fisher-Pearson formula heuristically, substituting membership functions for probability densities without a rigorous semantic bridge between the two. Our coefficient, in contrast, is grounded in an explicit probabilistic interpretation, making it both mathematically meaningful and aligned with the semantics of fuzzy set theory. We interpret a fuzzy number's left and right membership function components as cumulative and survival probability functions of associated two random variables $X_L$ and $X_R$. This yields a reading of its $\alpha$-cuts as generalized quantiles, i.e., intervals of values that are "at least $(1-\alpha)$-probable", highlighting a duality between probability and possibility theory. As a quantile-based measure, the coefficient is invariant under scale and location transformations. Its point-based variant needs only a fixed number of quantile evaluations, constant time in the $\alpha$-discretization, compared with the linear cost of moment-based alternatives. The coefficient comprises two complementary constituents: an "inner" measure quantifying the intrinsic skewness of the underlying probabilistic distributions, and an "outer" measure capturing the fuzzy number's overall profile asymmetry. We illustrate the measures within a fuzzy mean-variance-skewness portfolio optimization framework on historical equity data, comparing their performance with two of the most highly cited moment-based fuzzy skewness coefficients from the literature.
item.dc:creator: Jan Schneider, Kaja Bili\'nska, Paul Schneider, Tomasz Szanda{\l}a

item.title: Discrete Hyperbolic Cosecant Distributions
item.description: arXiv:2611.18913v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce three families of discrete hyperbolic cosecant probability distributions, supported either bilaterally on $\mathbb{Z}$ or unilaterally on $\mathbb{N}_0$, inspired by series evaluations of Srinivasa Ramanujan. We determine their exact normalization constants in terms of singular values of complete elliptic integrals and the Gaussian constant $G=\varpi/\pi$ with the lemniscate constant $\Gamma^2(1/4)/(2\sqrt{2\pi})$ by explicitly calculating some series, e.\,g. $$ \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} 2k \operatorname{cosech}(k \pi) = G^2 + \frac{1}{\pi}. $$ Furthermore, by connecting these distributions to Fourier transforms of powers of the hyperbolic secant and applying the Poisson summation formula, we obtain closed-form evaluations for even moments and hyperbolic secant lattice sums, e.\,g. $$ \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathrm{sech}^4(k \pi) = \frac{2}{3} \left(G^4 + G^2 + \frac{1}{\pi}\right) $$ as polynomials of the Gaussian constant.
item.dc:creator: Leonard J. E. Pleschberger
